openDecisions.question: Which DOM order should the single-instance Portrait, main column and Preview use, given that mobile shows Portrait first but desktop keeps them in one sticky sidebar?
openDecisions.specSays: 00 §3: one instance per block, solved with DOM/layout/order classes. 00 §2: one sticky sidebar with Portrait then Preview. 02 Accessibility: logical keyboard order.
options: A. DOM = [sidebar wrapper (Portrait, Preview), main]. The wrapper is 'contents' below lg and 'flex flex-col gap-6 sticky' at lg, with explicit grid placement (sidebar col 2, main col 1, both row 1). Preview is pushed after main on mobile with order classes. Mobile focus order equals visual order because Preview has nothing focusable; on desktop focus starts at the Portrait before the form.

B. DOM = [main, sidebar] as in Book Form, with Portrait pulled up via order-first on mobile. Desktop order matches Book, but on mobile the Portrait upload buttons are shown first and focused last, after the fixed action bar.
C. DOM = [Portrait, main, Preview] with per-item grid placement. Order is natural everywhere, but Portrait and Preview can no longer share one sticky wrapper.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: B is closest to book-form.tsx:795-1082. A adds one 'contents lg:flex' wrapper plus order and placement classes. C makes the sticky sidebar fragile.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It is the only option that keeps a single instance, one sticky sidebar, and focus order that matches the visual order on mobile. Use a div for the wrapper, because display:contents drops landmark semantics in some browsers, and give the Preview its own labelled region.
openDecisions.answeredBy: orchestrator, 2026-10-05: implementation-level fork inside the spec contract; CLAUDE-CODE-PROMPT forbids re-asking product questions the package settles, and each recommendation follows 00.

openDecisions.question: ActionRow truncates both title and subtitle to one line (action-row.tsx:145, :149). How should the long hide-presence hint (uk.json:8145, about 130 characters) be shown?
openDecisions.specSays: 00 §5: preferred pattern is title + subtitle/helper + trailing switch. 00 §6.6: hide-presence uses ActionRow. Truncation is not addressed.
options: A. Pass the hint as subtitle and accept a one-line ellipsis, which cuts it off on mobile and on most desktop widths.

B. ActionRow with title only, and the existing hint as a

directly under the row, linked to the Switch with aria-describedby.
C. Keep the subtitle and undo the truncation locally with descendant selectors in className, which couples Character code to ActionRow internals.
D. Add a wrapping option to components/ui/action-row.tsx. This edits a shared primitive in the folder CLAUDE.md §7 marks do-not-edit and goes outside the Character-only diff.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: B needs no primitive change and no new copy; C and D touch or depend on ActionRow internals.
openDecisions.recommendation: B. The full copy stays visible, ActionRow stays untouched, and 00 §5 only calls the subtitle pattern 'preferred'. Short labels like POV and the granular flags need no subtitle.
openDecisions.answeredBy: orchestrator, 2026-10-05: implementation-level fork inside the spec contract; CLAUDE-CODE-PROMPT forbids re-asking product questions the package settles, and each recommendation follows 00.

openDecisions.question: The spec says the granular spoiler flags 'remain collapsible' and the disclosure uses activeCount. Today the disclosure only expands and the count is never shown (character-edit-sections.tsx:350-396). What should the disclosure do?
openDecisions.specSays: 00 §6.6: 'granular flags remain collapsible', 'use current activeCount in disclosure UI'.
options: A. Keep the expand-only link button and add an activeCount badge to it. There is still no way to collapse.

B. A two-way disclosure: a Button with aria-expanded, or the existing components/ui/collapsible.tsx. It opens and closes, starts open when activeCount > 0, and shows an activeCount badge when the count is above 0.
openDecisions.copy: Showing the count needs copy: either a new characters.spoilers key with {count}, or a cross-namespace reuse of characters.card.hiddenFields 'Приховані поля: {count}' (uk.json:7861).
openDecisions.codebaseCost: Both are local to character-edit-sections.tsx. B also adds a collapse path that test :375 does not cover.
openDecisions.recommendation: B, with a new characters.spoilers count key. Keep the trigger's accessible name equal to 'Налаштувати, що саме приховати' when the count is 0, so test :375 holds, and expose the count as text when it is above 0.
openDecisions.answeredBy: orchestrator, 2026-10-05: implementation-level fork inside the spec contract; CLAUDE-CODE-PROMPT forbids re-asking product questions the package settles, and each recommendation follows 00.

openDecisions.question: What should the preview show as the name when the book display-name override exists but is blank?
openDecisions.specSays: 00 §8: name = book.displayName ?? global.name. Taken literally, a blank override shows an empty name and an empty avatar initial.
openDecisions.codeSays: toBookUpdate maps a blank override to null, meaning inherit (character-edit-form.ts:193, test character-edit-form.test.ts:52-58). The saved character will therefore show the global name.
options: A. Literal formula: a blank override renders an empty name.
B. Treat a trimmed-empty override as inherited and show global.name, mirroring what Save will store.
openDecisions.recommendation: B. The preview should predict the saved result, and the trim rule already exists in the model.
openDecisions.answeredBy: orchestrator, 2026-10-05: implementation-level fork inside the spec contract; CLAUDE-CODE-PROMPT forbids re-asking product questions the package settles, and each recommendation follows 00.

openDecisions.question: Who owns the portrait preview URL once the page needs it for the live preview?
openDecisions.specSays: 00 §7 allows a minimal CharacterImageField change to expose transient preview changes and to restore the global preview after reset. 01 puts the transient portrait preview state in character-edit-page.tsx. Neither says whether the field keeps its own copy.
options: A. Keep the internal previewUrl state, add an onPreviewChange callback and a fallback-URL prop for reset. The same URL then lives in both the field and the page.
B. Make the field's preview controlled: it receives the effective URL from the panel and reports upload success and reset. The page's transient state is the only source.
openDecisions.codebaseCost: After T13 the portrait panel is the only consumer (audit C38), so B breaks no other caller. B also fixes the reset-to-initial bug (audit C40) by construction.
openDecisions.recommendation: B. It keeps one source of truth (code-principles §5) and is still a minimal prop change.
